messages:
maya: quick sync — we need a pragmatic way to map kernel compatibility to cost/latency signals and use that for fallbacks. thinking: compatibility matrix + simple routing heuristic for Q sprint.

devin: +1. customer incidents show p99 tail spikes on long-seq flows when we use FP16 kernels with kv-prefetch. quantized kernels lower cost but sometimes regress quality.

sophia: what counts as a regression? do we want a single global threshold or per-customer eval sets?

maya: per-customer evals ideally. but MVP can use representative eval sets per workload class (chat, summarization, embeddings).

luke: propose a matrix: model_variant -> supported_kernels -> quant_levels -> expected_perf_delta. start small. I put a stub doc at <https://rwd/doc/kernel-matrix> (WIP).

chris: ops note: also capture KV cache hit rate sensitivity — fallback frequency skyrockets when hit < 20%.

runtime-bot: canary report: fused-attn kernel rolled to staging; median latency -8%, p99 -6% on short seqs.

maya: thanks. core questions for this thread: 1) what signals should trigger fallback? 2) how do we score cost vs quality? 3) what is MVP scope for this quarter?

devin: for signals: p99 (client-side), GPU util, token/sec, kv_hit_rate. Simple boolean rules to start: if p99 > 2x SLO OR gpu_util > 85% -> consider fallback.

sophia: quality scoring: start with eval-set delta metrics (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/KL) and also a heuristic token-level entropy delta. set conservative thresholds for degradations (KL > 0.08 as a starting point).

luke: implementational: runtime should emit metrics: `kernel_variant`, `fallback_reason`, `kv_hit_rate`, `ephemeral_quant_level`. Then a small rule engine in the router can switch to an alternative kernel or model variant.

chris: also add a counter metric: `fallbacks_per_minute` per route + per-customer to detect noisy fallbacks and tie to billing alerts.

maya: example rule snippet (MVP heuristic):
```
# pseudocode rule
if p99_ms > slo*2:
  if fallback_candidate.quant_level <= 4 and eval_delta(fallback_candidate) < threshold:
    route_to(fallback_candidate)  # e.g., int8 fused kernel
  else:
    route_to(compatible_model_variant)
```

devin: love the pseudocode. add a cooldown window and sampling for offline eval (we should sample some requests through the fallback path to verify quality).

sophia: sampling is critical. + we should run nightly regressions on customer eval sets after any kernel/quant change. Automation required.

luke: timeline ask: I can start kernel tagging and the matrix doc. need infra to expose kernel_variant in traces (should be a small change). estimate 2 dev-weeks.

chris: infra effort: adding metric + counter + tag is 3-4 infra days. alerting wiring another 2 days.

maya: OK MVP scope decision for this quarter (Q):
- deliver compatibility matrix (doc + mapping CSV)
- runtime metric tagging (`kernel_variant`, `fallback_reason`, `kv_hit_rate`)
- router rule engine (heuristic rules + cooldown + sampling)
- evaluation harness: nightly run against 3 eval sets
- alerting/counters for fallback rate
Scope notes: no global model re-training, no full A/B experiments in MVP.

devin: risks/unknowns: quant-quality for some LLMs unknown; may need quick model-specific QA and guardrails.

sophia: I'll provide 2 customer eval sets: retrieval-chat and long-form summarization. will also propose KL/ROUGE thresholds.

luke: action items agreed:
- luke: start matrix doc + kernel tagging PR (due in 3 working days)
- devin: write router heuristic spec + sampling plan + canary playbook (due next Tue)
- sophia: upload eval sets + thresholds (due next Fri)
- chris: infra alerts + `fallbacks_per_minute` metric (due end of sprint)

maya: blockers: we need prioritization from product — this could touch Dedicated customers (billing implications). @jay-ps (product) can you chime in?
jay-ps: saw offline. product aligns — this reduces customer-visible regressions and lowers unit cost. ok to prioritize as a medium bet. need an ROI blurb for stakeholders.

maya: ack. we'll prepare a one-pager quantifying expected cost savings (token-level) and incident reduction.

runtime-bot: reminder: perf sync moved to Thu 11am PST.

chris: small nit — please ensure the routing decision logs include request_id + sampled_response for traceability.

maya: agreed. final ask: any objections to the MVP scope?
chris: no objections. :thumbsup:

devin: no objections. will start spec.

sophia: fine with scope.

luke: ok from eng.

maya: thanks all — I'll consolidate notes into the matrix doc and tag owners. ping me if anything changes.

(three days later)

luke: PR opened: runtime tracing + `kernel_variant` tag. link: <https://rwd/pr/4821>. initial tests pass on staging.

devin: spec draft posted: <https://rwd/doc/fallback-spec>. includes cooldown, sampling 1% by default, and rollout steps.

sophia: eval sets uploaded to s3://rwd-evals/kernel-fallbacks. thresholds in the doc.

maya: moving this to a checklist for the sprint board. good work team.

(week later)

chris: canary data: fallback rate 0.8% on test routes, sampled checks show no measurable quality regression across sampled requests. will expand canary to 10% next week.

maya: excellent. closing this thread and moving to runway issue. will open a follow-up for post-canary metrics review.
